drivingQuestion: Is the mishna's ruling on the widow redundant?
outcomeNote: Needed lest one think a woman's unusual toil counts as an explicit declaration.

segments.he: פְּשִׁיטָא! מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: כֵּיוָן דְּלָאו דַּרְכַּהּ לְמִטְרַח, אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא פָּרֵישׁ – כְּמוֹ דְּפָרֵישׁ דָּמֵי, קָמַשְׁמַע לַן.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: Isn’t it «obvious» that the halakha in this case is the same as with regard to any other heir? The Gemara replies: It is necessary to state this, «lest you say» that «since it is not» a woman’s «way to toil» to enhance property, then «even though she did not expressly state» that she is toiling for herself, «it is considered as though» she «had expressly stated» this. The mishna «teaches us» that only if she expressly stated this do the profits accrue to her.

moves.about: the widow-heiress is like any other heir

moves.summary: Lest one think her unusual toil implies a declaration
moves.about: without the mishna one might think a woman's toil counts as if she declared it for herself
